description: South Carolina-only rules checked against the Code of Laws and SCDMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines. Section 56-5-1520 does not state a school-zone speed, so none is included.

questions.q: South Carolina's 70 mph maximum on the interstate system and other freeways is in force when
options: The highway has four lanes, even if no speed sign is posted
Official signs giving notice of that speed are posted
The driver is outside a city at night
questions.explanation: Section 56-5-1520(B)(1) sets seventy miles an hour on the interstate highway system and other freeways where official signs giving notice of this speed are posted. Section 56-5-1520(E) allows the limits in the section to be altered under sections 56-5-1530 and 56-5-1540.

questions.q: The maximum speed on a South Carolina multilane divided primary highway, where official signs give notice, is
questions.explanation: Section 56-5-1520(B)(2) sets sixty miles an hour on multilane divided primary highways where official signs giving notice of this speed limit are posted.

questions.q: Where section 56-5-1520 does not set a higher signed limit, the maximum in other locations is 55 mph, and unpaved roads are limited to
questions.explanation: Section 56-5-1520(B)(3) sets fifty-five miles an hour in other locations or on other sections of highways, and says unpaved roads are limited to forty miles an hour.

questions.q: The maximum speed in a South Carolina urban district is 30 mph. An urban district is territory built up with structures at intervals of less than 100 feet for a distance of
questions.explanation: Section 56-5-1520(C) says thirty miles an hour is the maximum speed in an urban district. It defines an urban district as territory contiguous to and including any street built up with structures devoted to business, industry, or dwelling houses situated at intervals of less than one hundred feet for a distance of a quarter of a mile or more.

questions.q: South Carolina's offense of driving with an unlawful alcohol concentration is an alcohol concentration of
options: Five one-hundredths of one percent or more
Eight one-hundredths of one percent or more
Two one-hundredths of one percent or more for every driver
Ten one-hundredths of one percent or more
questions.explanation: Section 56-5-2933(A) says it is unlawful for a person to drive a motor vehicle in this State while his alcohol concentration is eight one-hundredths of one percent or more.

questions.q: South Carolina requires the Department of Motor Vehicles to suspend, or refuse to issue, the license or permit of a driver under 21 who drives with an alcohol concentration of
options: Two one-hundredths of one percent or more
Eight one-hundredths of one percent or more only
Any concentration under two one-hundredths of one percent
Fifteen one-hundredths of one percent or more only
questions.explanation: Section 56-1-286(A) says the Department of Motor Vehicles shall suspend the driver's license, permit, or nonresident operating privilege of, or deny issuance to, a person under the age of twenty-one who drives a motor vehicle and has an alcohol concentration of two one-hundredths of one percent or more.

questions.q: For the South Carolina point system, a total of 12 points indicates disrespect for traffic laws. Twelve to fifteen points means a suspension of
questions.explanation: Section 56-1-740(A) says a total of twelve points assessed under section 56-1-720 indicates disrespect and disregard. The suspension periods are three months for 12 to 15 points, four months for 16 or 17, five months for 18 or 19, and six months for 20 or more. The department may suspend for not more than six months.

questions.q: A South Carolina beginner permit, conditional license, or special restricted license is suspended for six months for excessive points when the driver has accumulated
questions.explanation: The SCDMV points page says that if you hold a beginner's permit, conditional license, or special restricted driver's license and accumulate six or more points, driving privileges are suspended for six months for excessive points. Completing a defensive-driving course does not reinstate that suspension. Separately, points on a record are reduced by half after one year from the violation date.

provenance.manual: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles
provenance.section: Driver's license suspension for excessive points

questions.q: A South Carolina beginner's permit requires the applicant to be at least 15, and the permit must be held at least
questions.explanation: SCDMV form DMVB-35 says you must be at least 15 to get a beginner's permit and must hold it at least 180 days before applying for any type of license. From 6 a.m. to midnight the front-seat supervisor must be a licensed driver who is at least 21 and has at least one year of driving experience. After midnight the supervisor must be a licensed person listed on the Consent for Minor.

provenance.manual: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: A South Carolina driver under 17 who applies for a conditional or special restricted license must certify practice driving of
questions.explanation: DMVB-35 says a driver under 17 who applies for a conditional or special restricted license must practice with a licensed person listed on the Consent for Minor for at least 40 hours, including 10 hours during darkness, hold the beginner's permit at least 180 days, and meet the school-attendance rules on that form.

provenance.manual: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: A South Carolina conditional licensee may not transport more than two passengers under 21 unless a licensed driver who is at least 21 is in the vehicle. The brochure's exception is
options: Transporting family members, or students to and from school
Daylight driving only, with no other exception
questions.explanation: DMVB-35 says you cannot transport more than two passengers under 21 unless you are with a licensed driver who is at least 21. The only exception stated there is transporting family members or students to and from school. The same time and passenger restrictions apply to a special restricted license.

provenance.manual: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: DMVB-35 says the same time and passenger restrictions that apply to a conditional license also apply to a special restricted license. A waiver of the restricted hours requires proof from a parent or legal guardian and
options: Only a note from the driver
A school, work, church, or sports official
A doctor's note for any evening trip
questions.explanation: DMVB-35 says you must be 16 to request a waiver of the restricted times, and you must provide proof from your parent or legal guardian and your school official, employer, church official, or sports official that the hours interfere with school, work, church, or sports activities.

provenance.manual: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: After points are added in South Carolina, SCDMV reduces them by half
options: After one year from the violation
questions.explanation: The SCDMV points page says points are reduced by half after one year from the violation date on the ticket. Its example is four points received in June becoming two points in June of the next year.

provenance.manual: South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In South Carolina, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: South Carolina issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In South Carolina, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: South Carolina requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in South Carolina complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: South Carolina requires 40 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a South Carolina teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: South Carolina requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In South Carolina, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 15½ years.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the South Carolina car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the South Carolina car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Review - SCDMV Driver's License Practice Exam

questions.q: In South Carolina, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

questions.q: In South Carolina, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: South Carolina sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

questions.q: In South Carolina, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in South Carolina brings a suspension of 180 days.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a South Carolina residential district?
questions.explanation: South Carolina sets 30 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in South Carolina?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in South Carolina can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in South Carolina?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is South Carolina's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: South Carolina seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in South Carolina?
questions.explanation: South Carolina requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

questions.q: What is South Carolina's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: South Carolina requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

questions.q: Under South Carolina's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: South Carolina can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 12 months.
